File surface (read on `origin/main` `f0fdd45`; stop on a breach and explain it in the report):
- `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`: step 3 of `handleInstall` only. The registry's package door (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage` → `refuseSecurityCatalogNameConflicts`, ahead of every registry mutation) is already the one shared pre-write check for this rule, and every install door passes it. The cloud-fetched branch's lenient catch swallows its refusal and writes the ledger entry anyway. The fix: a `SecurityCatalogNameConflictError` that names an environment holder is refused on BOTH branches before the ledger write, with the error's own sentence (each colliding name and its holder), never tolerated. Every other register failure on the cloud branch keeps today's lenient answer.
- Tests: a new `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-catalog-name-collision.test.ts` over a real `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` registry: position, permission set and capability, inline and cloud-fetched branches, fresh install and upgrade, each refused with nothing registered and no ledger entry, plus a CONTROL per branch with no collision installing unchanged.
- `POST /api/v1/packages` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`): measure first. Its declaration parse (`PackageInstallManifestSchema`, the strict `ManifestSchema` close) is expected to refuse every catalog collection, so no catalog name reaches its registry write; if so, a pin in `packages/runtime/src` records it and the door's code is not touched.
- One `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, carrying the operator remedy for a deployment that already took such an upgrade.
- ⛔ Not `packages/objectql` (engine lane: the refusal, its message and the cold-boot check stay as they are), not `packages/spec`, not `plugin-security` (U2's access comparison is untouched).
Premise check owed before code: the card says the next cold boot refuses. On the tree, the marketplace rehydrate registers ledger entries at `kernel:ready`, after the engine's cold-boot check, and catches a register failure per entry. So the measured outcome may instead be "the boot runs, and the package (old version included) is not loaded". The report states which one a real restart shows; the fix is the same either way.
Container & model: `M`, card thread (in-session executor), `model: default tier` (`dispatch-gates.mjs --tier` on this surface: "no path-derived mandate"), `effort: high`
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Basis for the Clause-② line: nothing is widened. The cloud-fetched branch of `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` answered `200` (`hotLoaded: false`) for a package that ships a catalog name an environment-authored item holds, and now answers `422`, as the inline branch already does. That narrows the door's accept set. No metadata key, value or type changes.
Responsibility: the install door's own lenient register catch (`@objectstack/cloud-connection`) produces the risk · the registry's package-door refusal already covers it, and the inline branch honours it · reached by any administrator who upgrades a cloud-fetched marketplace package after cloning a vendor permission set or position under a name a later version ships.
Thread-read: none
Serial constraints cleared:
- No open PR touches `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` or `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (read across all 14 open PRs at claim time).
- PR #25355 (#24446 U2) on the same file is merged (`448374d3`); this card builds on it and leaves its step 2c alone.
